quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Merge.
Upcoming change in direction.

questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign means stop.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases.
As your speed increases, so should your following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 mph, survival is unlikely. Faster speeds mean longer stopping distances, so you need more space between you and the car ahead.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam lights. If visibility is too poor, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, check:

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the appropriate shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: You should not start across an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.
Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.

questions.explanation: Never enter an intersection unless you can clear it before the light turns red, even if the signal is green. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass if:

options.text: The vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.
The yellow line next to your side is broken.
The yellow line next to the opposite side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line next to your side is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: After a minor collision with no injuries and little damage, you should:

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
Not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: After a collision with no injuries or deaths, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.

questions.question: To know where traffic is behind you:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror regularly to stay aware of traffic behind you.

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, check:

options.text: The inside rearview mirror.
The outside rearview mirror.
Over your shoulders.

questions.explanation: Blind spots cannot be seen in your mirrors by definition. Look over your shoulders to check your blind spots.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger following distance.

questions.explanation: Keep a three- to four-second following distance behind motorcycles. They can stop quickly, and following too closely is dangerous. If a motorcyclist falls, you need extra distance to avoid hitting them. Falls are more likely on wet roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection?

options.text: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
Slow down and go carefully.
Stop completely and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red signal works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, check that oncoming traffic and pedestrians are clear, then proceed.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should your front wheels point?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the road edge
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.explanation: When parking downhill with no curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center so the car rolls into the curb instead.

questions.question: A child is about to run into the street. What should you do?

options.text: Start to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Sound a sharp horn blast.

questions.explanation: If a child or pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your car, sound a short, sharp horn blast. This warns them of the danger.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to prepare for the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before you turn left. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: This sign shows a railroad crossing with no signal. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely.
Drive at the same speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing marked with this sign, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains and be ready to stop if one is coming. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 pounds are allowed.
A hill is ahead.
A truck stop is ahead.

questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings and alert you to immediate dangers. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road and thaw out later. Be extra careful on bridges in cold weather, even if other roads look dry.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to a police officer?

options.text: Only after a crash.
After a crash or when stopped for a ticket.
Only when stopped for a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a crash or when stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. An officer can ask to see it after a traffic stop or crash. You must show your insurance proof and driver's license upon request.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic flows in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: The car ahead of you is stopped at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Carefully pass at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and go only after all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and go only after all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Never pass a stopped car at a crosswalk. Pedestrians you cannot see may be crossing. Stop and wait until all pedestrians have safely crossed before going.

questions.question: What message is on this yellow pennant-shaped sign?

options.text: Right turns only.
Right turns permitted.
No passing zone.

questions.explanation: Yellow pennant-shaped signs mark a no passing zone.

questions.question: When driving in snow or icy conditions, what should you do?

options.text: It is safe to use your cruise control.
Change speed and direction slowly and gradually.
Drive as you would in normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change speed and direction slowly and gradually.
questions.explanation: In snow or ice, change speed and direction slowly. Do not use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may slip and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.explanation: Alcohol damages all the abilities you need to drive safely. It affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and skill.

questions.question: What do drivers need to safely drive on interstate highways?

options.text: The ability to safely drive at higher speeds.
Constant attention.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe driving on the interstate requires you to stay alert and be able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear from the truck driver's view or are so close that they prevent the driver from stopping and turning safely.
Areas where cars have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Areas where cars have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear from the truck driver's view or are so close that they prevent the driver from stopping and turning safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars disappear into the truck's blind spots. They can also be areas where cars are so close to the truck that they make it hard for the driver to stop and turn safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.
